clue.text: Not even a Stock Exchange employee but a casual worker

parts.note: a number that is not even is odd
a jobber was a dealer on the London Stock Exchange floor, trading shares with brokers

explanation.surface: A man who is neither a City trader nor regularly employed picks up casual work.
explanation.walkthrough: A JOBBER was a type of dealer on the London Stock Exchange until 1986.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes odd jobs is a casual labourer doing piecework as it comes.

clue.text: Moved suddenly and had the courage to take their leader

indicators.note: the word for courage is made to take another letter inside it

parts.note: to have the courage to do something is to have dared

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter of their is used

explanation.surface: Someone bravely lunged forward to seize the head of a rival group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take' puts T, the leader of 'their', inside DARED.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart is to move with a quick sudden dash.

clue.text: Jack at home, cross,'e'd been beset with bad luck

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
someone at home is in
a cross is drawn as the letter X
the dropped-aitch spelling of he'd sounds as ed, written ED

explanation.surface: A cross Cockney called Jack, stuck at home, complains he has been dogged by misfortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'e'd is how a Cockney speaker, dropping the H, says he'd, giving ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be jinxed is to be under a curse that keeps bringing misfortune.

clue.text: He is in supreme command

indicators.note: says the pronoun sits within the word for supreme

parts.note: the supreme option is the best one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is the commander-in-chief, holding the highest authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' puts HE inside BEST, splitting it as BE-HE-ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is an order or instruction, as in acting at someone's bidding.

clue.text: Bridge opponents and bridge partners are to become entangled

parts.note: at bridge East and North sit side by side and play against each other
at bridge South and North sit opposite each other and play as partners
taken as written

explanation.surface: At the card table, rivals and partners end up hopelessly tangled together.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players are named by compass points: N-S partner E-W, so E and N are opponents while S and N are partners.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare is to catch in a trap or net, tangling something up.

clue.text: Domineering and irreverent about the Queen

indicators.note: the word for irreverent goes about, that is around, the royal letters

parts.note: an irreverent person lacks piety, so is impious
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: An overbearing person speaks disrespectfully of the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ER, the Queen's cipher, inside IMPIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An imperious manner is arrogant and commanding, expecting to be obeyed.

clue.text: One at the lodge to release mother and child

parts.note: to release is to free
ma is an informal word for mother
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A lodge member arranges for a mother and her child to be let go.
explanation.walkthrough: A lodge is the local meeting-house of a Masonic branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Masonic fraternity meet in local branches called lodges.

clue.text: Speculated about what the birds did

definitions.meaning: placed a small gamble, a usage from British betting slang
flapped wings rapidly, as birds do on taking off

explanation.surface: Someone guessed idly at the movements of the birds.
explanation.walkthrough: To have a flutter is British slang for a small bet, so 'fluttered' means gambled.
explanation.definitionFit: Placing a small wager is having a flutter; birds flapping their wings quickly also do this.

clue.text: Unprincipled scholar returns for the exam

indicators.note: the degree letters are said to come back, read from right to left

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate scholar
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A dishonest academic comes back to sit the viva.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns MA round to AM before ORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without morals has no principles of right and wrong.

clue.text: In the country, head of house is right to vote

indicators.note: the letters from house and is go into the name of the country

parts.note: France is a European country

indicators.note: the head is the top, so the opening letter of house is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A householder abroad discovers they are entitled to cast a ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts H (head of house) and IS inside FRANCE: FRANC-HIS-E.
explanation.definitionFit: The franchise is the legal entitlement to take part in elections.

clue.text: Show displeasure at being partly misrepresented

indicators.note: only a part of the following word is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed at having their views distorted.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitter indignation about it.

clue.text: The piper who picked to mock heavy ribbon

parts.note: Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled pepper in the tongue-twister
to mock as an adjective means fake, a sham

explanation.surface: A tongue-twister hero is teased about some ribbon.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Piper is the hero of an English tongue-twisting nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Petersham is a thick corded ribbon used for hatbands and waistbands.

clue.text: Speak at length in elaborate detail

indicators.note: something elaborate is worked out intricately, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A speaker holds forth, going into every particular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elaborate' reads as an adjective but signals the anagram of DETAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilate on a subject is to expound on it fully and expansively.

clue.text: Frank took in an examinee

parts.note: frank means open and honest, candid
to take food in is to eat it, so took in is ate

explanation.surface: A man called Frank deceived a student sitting a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name, and 'took in' like 'deceived'.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate is someone sitting an examination or seeking a post.

clue.text: Lupin left wild in abundance

indicators.note: the letters are allowed to run wild into a different order

explanation.surface: A garden flower has been allowed to grow unchecked everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges LUPIN and LEFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plentiful exists in large quantities, more than enough.

clue.text: Made known that the lady carried little weight before start of delivery

indicators.note: places the earlier pieces ahead of the letter that follows

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name
an ounce is a small unit of weight

indicators.note: the start is the opening letter of delivery

explanation.surface: It was revealed that a woman was very light when about to give birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of delivery' is D; 'delivery' suggests childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce is to make public or proclaim.

clue.text: Busy worker has most of the drink

indicators.note: means nearly all of the word for drink is kept, its final letter lost

parts.note: beer is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A hard-working employee knocks back nearly all the alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker honeybees are proverbially busy, as in busy as a bee.

clue.text: Fly-by-night cricketer?

definitions.meaning: a creature that flies by night, the nocturnal flying mammal
a cricketer who wields the ..., a batsman

explanation.surface: Is the unreliable chap a cricketer?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly-by-night' usually means a shady, untrustworthy person; cricket's batsman is commonly called a bat.
explanation.definitionFit: The nocturnal flying mammal comes out after dark; in cricket a batsman is often called a bat.

clue.text: Expedition leader has energy and self-conceit

indicators.note: the leader comes first, so only the opening letter of Expedition is used

parts.note: go means vigour, energy

explanation.surface: The head of an expedition is full of vigour and vanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes E from 'Expedition'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflated ego is an excessive sense of self-importance.

clue.text: Greek maiden losing article in Georgia

indicators.note: the maiden's name is said to lose a piece

parts.note: Atalanta was the swift-footed huntress of Greek myth
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A mythical Greek girl drops something while in the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes A from ATALANTA.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of the US state of Georgia is a place in Georgia.

clue.text: Stick round island obtaining some sugar

indicators.note: the word for stick is placed round the island

parts.note: glue is what makes things stick
Cos (Kos) is a Greek island

explanation.surface: Gluing things around an island gets you a sweet substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts COS, the Greek island, inside GLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Glucose is a simple sugar that is the body's main energy source.

clue.text: It would hold a very small number

definitions.text: It would hold a very small number

parts.words: It would hold a very small number
parts.note: a numeral that really is small, ..., though the clue suggests a container with little capacity

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like something with tiny capacity; really the answer is a very small number.
explanation.definitionFit: The numeral after one is about as small a number as there is.

clue.text: Her wimp produced 8 plaintive cry

indicators.note: the letters are produced in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A feeble man of hers lets out a pitiful sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' rearranges HER and WIMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimper is a low, feeble cry of pain or distress.

clue.text: Two boys found in the central tower

parts.note: Don is a boy's name
Jon is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A pair of lads are discovered in the castle's keep.
explanation.definitionFit: A donjon is the keep, the strongest central tower of a castle.

clue.text: Pieces of rubbish tossed a brides

indicators.note: letters tossed about land in a different order

explanation.surface: Wedding confetti thrown at brides leaves litter behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossed' rearranges BRIDES; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered fragments and rubbish left over.

clue.text: Thanks non-drinker with spectacles for the design

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
TT, teetotal, describes someone who does not drink alcohol
OO looks like a pair of spectacles

explanation.surface: A teetotaller wearing glasses expresses gratitude for a drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thanks; OO resembles a pair of glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is a design inked into the skin.

clue.text: You and I have the wrong beetle

parts.note: you and I together are we
wrong in the moral sense is evil

explanation.surface: Two people realise they have identified the insect incorrectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Weevils are a large family of small, snouted beetles.

clue.text: One placing explosives in pit stratum

parts.note: a mine is a pit dug for coal or ore
a stratum is a layer of rock

explanation.surface: A demolition worker sets charges in a coal seam.
explanation.definitionFit: A minelayer is a vessel or aircraft that lays explosive mines.

clue.text: Lowers oneself as one thinks fit

definitions.meaning: condescends to do something beneath one
considers it suitable or worthy to do

explanation.walkthrough: 'as one' is a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to condescend, consenting to do something as if it were beneath one's dignity, which also means judging it fitting.

clue.text: Skilled worker in force

definitions.meaning: a trained machine hand or artisan
in effect, as a law or rule currently applying

explanation.walkthrough: 'in force' reads like a police or army link but is the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory machinist is called an operative; a rule in effect is operative.

clue.text: Holidaymaker in an open-topped car

definitions.meaning: an open car with a folding roof built for touring

explanation.walkthrough: 'in an' is a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist on the road is a tourer, and an open motorcar made for long trips has the same name.

clue.text: Old Greek totaliser was confusing

indicators.note: the letters were confused into a new order

explanation.surface: An ancient philosopher found the betting machine baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was confusing' rearranges TOTALISER, a betting machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the classical Greek philosopher, pupil of Plato.
